message.content: **Summary:** I read Walmart's latest 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-01-31) and checked the live quote ($69.96 last, $69.94/$69.98 bid-ask), then bought WMT. The filing showed a business improving on both the top and bottom line: net sales of $648,125M versus $611,289M the prior year (~6% growth), operating income of $27,012M versus $20,428M (~32% growth), net income of $15,511M versus $11,680M, diluted EPS of $1.91 versus $1.42, and net cash from operating activities of $35,726M — evidence of margin expansion and strong cash generation, with management stating liquidity is sufficient for at least the next twelve months. I placed a single buy limit order for 71 shares at $69.98 (the current ask), which filled at $69.98 for roughly $4,969 — within the $5,000 per-order cap and the $10,000 daily total, and well inside the $50,000 cash balance. No funds were moved out of the account, and I made no NVDA trades, so the mandate's constraints were all respected.
